subject: Vendor retention exception & evidence compactification request
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@verihealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: vendor-security@verihealth.com
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: retention exception + CAIQ fragment upload guidance

Hi Ben / Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We (VeriHealth) are progressing through our vendor intake and have a couple of asks where we could use help from Redwood's portal team. TL;DR: we have a retention exception for a small set of logs (access and auth metadata) and the SIG/CAIQ payloads we can provide are fragmented across multiple exports. Our security ops team prefers a compacted evidence bundle to avoid repeatedly re-uploading similar artifacts.

Specifics:
- Evidence: CAIQ answers exported on 2027-08-10; we split out network/cert items and IAM/access logs as separate files.
- Retention: We need a documented retention-exception acceptance from the vendor (you) to accept 6 months instead of our default 12 months for the sample logs. The rest of the CAIQ must remain at standard retention.
- Portal: We'll upload a zipped bundle if Whistic/Vendr will accept a single zip with a manifest file. If the portal requires per-file mapping we can rename, but it's more work on our side.

Attached: a small sample of the access logs and a compacted CAIQ fragment bundle for review.

Can you confirm whether Vendr/Whistic supports a manifest-based bundle, and if Redwood can sign off on the retention exception? If there's a preferred manifest schema we can use that.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Security Program Manager | VeriHealth
[attachment: verihealth_caiq_fragments_2027.zip (zip, 8.1MB)]
[attachment: access_logs_sample.csv (csv, 45KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@verihealth.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: retention exception + CAIQ fragment upload guidance

Thanks Samantha — appreciate the context and the sample artifacts. Short answer: Vendr/Whistic can accept a single bundle if the manifest is present and we map the manifest entries during ingestion. A couple of notes: 

- The retention exception is not solely a portal decision; we need compliance sign-off (cc'ing Olivia from Compliance).
- For evidence mapping we generally ask for a small JSON or CSV manifest that includes filename, CAIQ section id, and a short description. If you can provide that in the zip as manifest.csv that will speed ingestion and indexing.

Olga — can you take point on confirmation for our ingestion pipeline and draft the acceptance language for the 6-month exception? Once Mina signs off we can attach a short statement to the vendor profile.

Ben
Ben Carter
Vendor Onboarding Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: retention exception + CAIQ fragment upload guidance

Mina / Marissa — forwarding VeriHealth's ask. Attached are the sample files they uploaded and Ben's note.

Questions for compliance:
1) Is a 6-month retention for the sample access logs acceptable from a SOC 2 / customer expectation perspective if we record the exception on the vendor profile and require a signed attestation?
2) Do we need to collect additional provenance (S3 object metadata, upload timestamp) to record defensibly?

Operational ask for portal team: if we accept a zip + manifest.csv format what minimal fields must the manifest contain so that our ingestion job can map the CAIQ fragments to SIG sections and preserve links in the profile? My proposal (for discussion): filename, sha256, caiq_section, short_description, retention_override_months (optional).

I've attached a mock manifest template and the two sample files from VeriHealth. If compliance signs off I'll reply-all with an acceptance statement they can attach on the vendor profile and give the greenlight for ingestion.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Technical Program Manager, Security Integrations | Redwood Inference
[attachment: manifest_template.csv (text, 1KB)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: retention exception + CAIQ fragment upload guidance

Olga / Ben — thanks for the clear summary and the artifacts. I reviewed the sample logs and the proposed manifest schema. Compliance position: we are comfortable approving a limited 6-month retention exception for the specific access_logs_sample.csv sample set provided the following controls are in place and documented on the vendor profile: 

- Explicit exception statement attached to the VeriHealth vendor record listing the affected artifact names and the 6-month retention window.
- A signed attestation from VeriHealth acknowledging the shorter retention for those artifacts.
- Preserve object provenance: require upload timestamps and SHA256 in the manifest (we need this for audit traceability).
- Scoped indexing: the rest of CAIQ content remains at standard retention and cannot be included under the exception.

Olga, please use the language below and attach it to the profile once VeriHealth provides the signed attestation. Also confirm that ingestion will respect manifest.sha256 and manifest.retention_override_months.

Acceptance language (copy-paste):
Redwood Inference approves a retention exception for specified access logs submitted by VeriHealth. The exception reduces retention for the listed artifacts to 6 months from the date of upload. This exception applies only to artifacts explicitly listed in the vendor profile manifest and does not alter retention for any other evidence or CAIQ sections. VeriHealth must provide a signed attestation acknowledging the reduced retention window. Redwood will retain manifest metadata (including SHA256 and upload timestamp) for audit purposes.

Once you have the attestation we can mark the profile and proceed with ingestion.

-Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Compliance & Privacy | Redwood Inference
